To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
highly porous columnar ceria structures can be grown on single crystal yttria-stabilized zirconia by pulsed laser deposition and exhibit superior performance as solid oxide fuel cell electrodes.

highly porous, vertically oriented ceria films with a high surface-to-volume-ratio and high porosity can be grown by pulsed laser deposition and exhibit a significantly reduced interfacial reaction impedance for hydrogen electrooxidation in comparison to conventional ceria thin films.
the electrochemical reaction resistance of ceria-based electrodes can be significantly reduced by the formation of nanostructured columnar structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of novel porous ceria films with highly porous, columnar architecture for use as high-performance solid oxide fuel cell electrodes.
the fabrication and investigation of highly porous, nanostructured, column-shaped Sm0.2Ceo.8O1+δ films as an anode material for solid oxide fuel cell applications.
the fabrication of high performance ceria-based solid oxide fuel cell electrodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nanostructured, column-shaped morphology of the ceria films is responsible for the high electrode activity, as a result of the large surface area and the high porosity of the electrode structure.
a highly porous, nanostructured ceria film with vertically oriented morphology is a promising material for high-performance solid oxide fuel cell electrodes.
the highly porous, columnar morphology of Sm0.2 Ce0.8O2−δ films grown by pulsed laser deposition is a key factor for the high activity of these films as solid oxide fuel cell electrodes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
highly porous, vertically oriented ceria films with a columnar architecture are a promising candidate for a solid oxide fuel cell electrode.
nanostructured, highly porous ceria films with columnar morphology can be used as a high-performance anode for solid oxide fuel cell applications.
nanostructuring of the ceria anode is a viable approach to enhance electrode activity for solid oxide fuel cell operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the high surface-to-volume electrode structure of the films is responsible for the low interfacial reaction resistances observed, and that these low resistances are maintained even at high operating temperatures.
nanostructured, highly porous columnar films can provide a high surface-to-volume electrode structure, which is essential for high-performance SOFC operation.
the electrode reaction impedance for hydrogen electro-oxidation is strongly dependent on the electrode structure and can be significantly reduced by nanostructuring of the oxide material.
